ogTitle: Issaquah Tile Installation, Specified Like a Modern Remodel
ogDesc: From Highlands new-builds to in-town originals: large-format porcelain, curbless entries, and a bonded waterproofing membrane that passes a photographed 24-hour flood test before tile. (425) 595-1079.

roles.heroLead: Waterproof is a property of the membrane, not the tile — grout never held water out of anything. In a Highlands new-build with a curbless master or an older in-town Issaquah bathroom, that layer is the line between a twenty-year shower and a $40,000 framing repair. Assembly first, a 24-hour flood test on camera, then the first tile.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Issaquah, WA?
roles.costP1: In Issaquah, installed tile runs about $14–$26 per square foot once tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor are totaled — the labor component starts at $11/sq ft on its own. A tub-shower surround in the standard size prices at $3,200–$6,800; a full bathroom — floor, shower, niche — generally finishes between $6,500 and $14,000.
roles.costP2: The detail most estimates gloss over: format drives labor harder than the per-box price does. Large-format porcelain at $12 can install for less than $4 mosaic sheet, since the hours live in the cuts and grout lines rather than on the invoice.
roles.costNote: Installed ranges for Issaquah homes as of August 2026, covering tile, materials and labor. The written figure from your free on-site estimate is the one to plan on.
roles.layersLead: Bottom to top, seven layers. Each failed shower we get called into around Issaquah left one out — the membrane, nearly every time — a few hundred dollars saved during construction, five figures spent tearing it open later.
roles.whyP1: Shower leaks work quietly. Moisture gets past grout, loads the substrate, and two years on you notice a soft spot in the hall or a ceiling stain in the room below. The fix at that stage isn't tile — it's framing, subfloor, drywall and the entire shower rebuilt.
roles.whyP2: Call waterproofing 10% of the shower's price. There is no cheaper insurance in a bathroom remodel, and no costlier thing to leave out.
roles.scopeIntro: Starting numbers below — tile format, what we find in the substrate, and layout complexity all move them. The exact price goes on paper at your house, free.
roles.cardShower: The full waterproofed build: pre-sloped base, bonded membrane, documented flood test, then niche, curb or curbless threshold, then tile. The invisible half is the half that matters.
roles.cardFloors: Bathrooms, kitchens, entries, mudrooms and basements — subfloor brought flat, with an uncoupling membrane specified wherever movement or radiant heat requires it.
roles.cardBacksplash: Slab-look porcelain, herringbone, subway or mosaic sheet. Outlet cuts, edge profiles, and a grout color chosen against the counter instead of the tile box.
roles.cardHeated: Electric radiant mat set over an uncoupling layer, resistance-verified before setting and again after, on a dedicated circuit. Worth specifying only while the floor is open anyway.
roles.cardRepair: Cracked tiles, crumbling grout, loose corners in the shower. We tell you plainly whether a repair solves it or the substrate beneath has already let go.
roles.cardDemo: Existing tile, thinset and backer removed, dust managed with sheeting and negative air, everything hauled off site. Your garage and driveway stay yours.

roles.daysLead: Four to six working days covers a typical Issaquah bathroom. The two days nobody budgets for are the waterproofing days — the ones the shower depends on.
roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Issaquah, WA?
roles.faqA1: Installed tile in Issaquah prices out at roughly $14 to $26 per square foot, with tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor included; labor starts around $11 per square foot by itself. Standard tub-shower surrounds land at $3,200 to $6,800, and complete bathrooms — floor, shower and niche — typically total $6,500 to $14,000. Format is the real price lever: mosaic sheets and large-format both consume far more labor per square foot than a basic 12×12 field tile.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Issaquah?
roles.faqA2: Budget $3,200 to $6,800 for a standard alcove shower in Issaquah. That covers demolition, the bonded waterproofing system, a pre-sloped pan or base, setting, a niche and grout. Curbless thresholds — popular in newer Highlands remodels — plus benches, steam showers and full-height stone sit above the range. The waterproofing itself is around a tenth of the price and prevents the failure that runs into tens of thousands.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Yes, on every job, and to a written standard: a pre-sloped base, sheet or liquid membrane taken up the walls, corners, seams and pipe penetrations sealed, then a 24-hour flood test that gets documented before tile is set. Cement board plus thinset is not waterproofing. Tile and grout pass water; the bonded membrane behind them is the only layer protecting your framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Count on four to six working days for an Issaquah bathroom. Day one is demolition and dust containment; the next is substrate work and waterproofing, followed by the 24-hour flood test; setting takes one to two days; the last day is grout, silicone and trim. Give the grout another 24 hours to cure before using the shower. A standalone floor is normally a one-to-two-day job.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Specify porcelain wherever there's water or foot traffic: denser body, under 0.5% water absorption, better chip resistance. Ceramic earns its spot on walls and backsplashes at a lower price. In Issaquah our default is porcelain for all floors and shower floors, with ceramic or glass reserved for vertical surfaces where looks are the whole job.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes. Figure $11 to $16 per square foot installed for an electric radiant mat with thermostat — and since it only makes sense while the floor is already open, it's the cheapest genuine upgrade an Issaquah bathroom can get. The mat is laid over an uncoupling membrane, resistance-tested twice — before setting and after — and wired to its own circuit.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Usually. Removal with haul-away prices at about $3.50 per square foot, and it buys you the only clear view of the subfloor — checking for rot, movement or old moisture — while keeping the finished height right where floors meet at doorways. On a flat, sound, well-bonded surface, tiling over tile is technically possible, but it raises the floor and conceals exactly the problems better found at demolition than after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Issaquah?
roles.faqA8: A kitchen backsplash in Issaquah runs $1,100 to $2,200 installed for the usual 30 square feet, including outlet cuts, edge trim and grout matched to the counter. Layout-heavy choices push toward the top: herringbone, mosaic sheets, a picture-frame accent behind the range, or slab-look porcelain carried to the ceiling — cutting and setting time is what moves the number.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often, yes. Repair and regrout work begins at $8 per square foot — the right scope when grout has stained or started crumbling, an impact cracked a couple of tiles, or shower corners need grout cut out and re-done in silicone. The exception is substrate failure: hollow-sounding tiles, tiles loosening in a pattern, or soft wall sections mean a repair buys months at best. We diagnose which case yours is before we write a number.
roles.faqQ10: Which Issaquah neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: Every part of Issaquah — Issaquah Highlands, Olde Town, Talus, Klahanie, Squak Mountain, Montreux, Providence Point, Gilman, North Issaquah, South Cove, Sycamore and Mirrormont, out to Preston, High Point and May Valley — plus Sammamish, Bellevue, Newcastle, Renton, Snoqualmie and the wider Eastside into Seattle.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Tile installation carries a 2-year workmanship warranty from OC Flooring — longer than our carpet coverage, because a tile defect tends to appear in year two, not week two. Install a manufacturer's full waterproofing assembly and its system warranty stacks on top of ours. The membrane and the flood test are both photographed, so a documented record exists for any future sale of the house.
roles.hoodsOut: Not seeing your area? Anywhere within roughly an hour of Issaquah is workable — mention it when you book.
